thread:
maria: FYI I'm prototyping a 'Grafana Shepherd' panel set to surface cross-region GPU thermal fingerprints + SLO impact. Want to capture ECC/Xid bursts, nvlink jitter, and the cascade to drains.
devin: Love the name :sheep: Quick Q — do you want one dashboard per-region + an aggregated view, or just an aggregated rollup with region selectors?
maria: Aggregated rollup + per-region drilldown. Main thing is making causal links obvious: e.g., ECC spike -> increased retries -> degraded tail latency -> forced drains.
jae: Make sure we show the per-card 'heat signature' over time. Seen cases where cards in rack A have subtle repeated 2-3C spikes pre-failure. Could be airflow / fan curve.
sandeep: Agree. Also include a smoothed anomaly band so ops doesn't get paged on noise. Maybe a 7d baseline and then a 1h deviation detector.
lucy: Also want cost context on the same page. Replacement vs patching math. If we replace N cards/year, how does that affect monthly cost vs outage minutes saved?
maria: Good call. Thinking of tiles: Thermal trend, ECC/Xid timeline, NVLink/PCIe error heatmap, drain frequency, and cost-effectiveness gauge.
devin: For NVLink jitter we can use percentiles over packet latency. Example query (Prometheus + node exporter metrics):
```promql
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(nvlink_packet_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, gpu_id, region))
```
That gives per-GPU tail latency.
jae: For Xid/ECC correlation I was plotting cumulative counters then overlaying QPS to see if it's load-related. Quick snippet:
```promql
increase(nv_gpu_xid_errors_total[1h]) by (gpu_id)
increase(nv_gpu_ecc_correctable_total[1h]) by (gpu_id)
```
Plot them with a shared time axis.
monitoring-bot: Alert snapshot: `gpu-ecc-burst-prod-us-west` fired at 2026-03-07T12:04:11Z on rack-12 (3 GPUs with >50 ECC corrections in 10m). Link: https://graf.redwood/gpu/alerts/987
maria: That's the pattern — bursts that cluster on a rack. Shepherd should highlight rack co-occurrence and nearby ambient temp trends.
sandeep: Triage note: when we see rack-coincident bursts, prefer a soft-drain (mark unschedulable + cordon) and run a repeated ECC stress test before full replacement. Saves replacements for transient thermal issues.
lucy: We also need an "auto-fallback policy" widget showing how routing should shift (cross-region fallbacks) when a region's effective GPU capacity drops below SLO threshold. Shows cost delta (eg cross-region egress + spot price diff).
devin: UX idea: a small interactive timeline where clicking an ECC spike shows the following 60m of tail-latency, queued requests, and any drain events.
jae: Could we add a simple ML-based predictor? Feed last 72h of thermal + ECC + nvlink counters per-GPU and output risk score. Display as a sparkline and an action recommendation: monitor / soft-drain / replace.
maria: Risk model is good but keep the first release rule-based. We'll do a stacked scoring approach: thermal anomalies (0-3), ECC burst frequency (0-4), nvlink jitter (0-2), each normalized to 0-1 then weighted.
sandeep: For runbooks, add a small popover with the exact CLI steps:
```
# soft drain
kubectl cordon node-gpu-XX
kubectl drain node-gpu-XX --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=120
# stress test
sudo nv_gpu_diag --ecc-stress --duration 600
```
lucy: I'll work with finance to estimate per-card TCO inputs. We need avg replacement cost, shipping lead time, and incident minute cost by region.
devin: Implementation notes: create a new grafana folder `gpu-shepherd` with panels as JSON templates. Use Loki for logs and link panels to the last 200 lines of dmesg / nvidia-smi.
maria: Action items: (1) dev -> grafana folder scaffold + sample queries (devin). (2) SRE -> runbook + soft-drain recipe (sandeep). (3) Observability -> add rack co-occurrence alert (jae). (4) Finance -> TCO numbers (lucy). I'll draft the panel wireframe and PR.
devin: I'll open the grafana PR tonight, include dashboard JSON + example Prometheus queries.
jae: I'll prototype the per-card heat-sparkline and co-occurrence calc. Thinking co-occurrence = count of GPUs in rack with ECC > threshold in rolling 10m.
sandeep: I'll update the runbook and add the stress-test automation snippet.
lucy: Sending TCO inputs by EOD tomorrow.
maria: Nice. Let's avoid creating an alert storm — initial release will be read-only with annotation flags, then enable alerts after one week of sampling. Thanks everyone.
monitoring-bot: Noted. I'll mute related alert notifications for the shepherd-testing namespace for 7 days when the dash is deployed.
maria: Will post PR link when ready.
